clue.text: Going in, as poorly and fretting

indicators.note: poorly suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone heading in, feeling unwell and worried about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' looks like a description of health but signals rearranging the nine letters of 'Going in, as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: agonising over something is fretting about it in torment.

clue.text: Primate must welcome son in this section of church

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A monkey or ape being let into part of a church to greet a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted, usually semicircular, recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Working around the setter is a sign

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
the setter refers to the crossword compiler, so me

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's daily toil is taken as a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter' is the compiler speaking of themself: ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a portent or augury is taken as a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: I married and went white, transfixed

parts.note: to pale is to go white in the face

explanation.surface: A bride confessing she wed and blanched, frozen in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something transfixed is pierced right through, as if on a stake.

clue.text: Spiteful when bishop leaves, causing irritation

indicators.note: leaves means the named letter departs from the word

parts.note: a spiteful remark is a bitchy one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A nasty cleric whose departure irritates everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An itchy jumper or rash causes the urge to scratch, a kind of skin irritation.

clue.text: Lacking time, flier got ID forged and inflated

indicators.note: lacking says the letter for time is missing from the pool
forged means made up or counterfeited, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An airline passenger short of time fakes identity papers and feels puffed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' takes T out of FLIERGOTID; 'forged' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a glorified version is an inflated or exaggerated one, made out grander than it is.

clue.text: Quick runs help around start of play

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes outside the second

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fast scoring with assistance at the start of a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rapid and quick both describe great speed.

clue.text: Got up with it for such fruit

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, so got up
someone hip is fashionable or with it

explanation.surface: Getting up and being trendy, all for the sake of a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such fruit' points back at the clue's own pieces: the fruit of the plant named in the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the red fruit of the rose plant, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: Rural type in favour of French wine agents left

parts.note: pro means in favour of
vin is the French word for wine
the CIA is the US agency of intelligence agents

explanation.surface: A country person who supports French wine while spies have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A provincial is a person from the provinces, outside the capital, often seen as unsophisticated.

clue.text: Writer on board covered by log — get medication here

indicators.note: covered by means the inner part sits within the outer one

parts.note: a log is a daily record, a diary

indicators.note: on here means aboard, so the writer goes inside the vessel's letters

parts.note: with on, board means a steamship one boards, abbreviated SS
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A ship's log reveals a writer aboard who knows where to find medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is a crossword convention: inside the steamship letters. 'covered by' then sets that result inside the log.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is a room or shop where medicines are prepared and handed out.

clue.text: Extent of blubber on lass's rear?

indicators.note: on places the piece named before it in front of the one named next in this across clue
rear picks the back letter of the word

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily, to weep

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about how much fat sits on a girl's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like fat but is the verb to cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the sweep of something is its range or extent, as in the broad sweep of a landscape.

clue.text: Yields on hybrid weapons

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the first-named piece after the second

parts.note: a hybrid is a cross between breeds
to yield is to bow, give way

explanation.surface: Hybrid crops and their yields used as weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbows are medieval bows mounted on a stock, firing bolts: examples of weapons.

clue.text: Live dangerously and shoot after drama

indicators.note: after says the words before it follow the piece named next

parts.note: a play is a drama
with means along with, and
to fire is to shoot

explanation.surface: Taking risks and gunning things down after the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to play with fire is to take foolish risks, to live dangerously.

clue.text: Like some accounts maybe, one-sided

definitions.meaning: ledger accounts whose debits and credits do not match

explanation.surface: Biased reports or lopsided books of account.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbalanced books fail to tally; an unbalanced argument is lopsided or biased.

clue.text: Skill that sees cast get far, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A theatrical talent that might take actors a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagecraft is skill in writing or staging plays, a theatrical expertise.

clue.text: Famously, how Bach perhaps composed?

definitions.meaning: in a celebrated or well-known way
a whimsical sense: in the manner of musical notes, as a composer writes

explanation.surface: A question about the great composer's working method.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as NOTED plus -LY: by means of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Notedly means in a celebrated or remarkable manner, the same as famously.

clue.text: Horses? The old dears head off

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

indicators.note: head off removes the opening letter

parts.note: dears and darlings are terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Horses ask whether old ladies are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' drops D from DARLINGS; YE is the old way of writing THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearlings are horses (or other animals) in their second year; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Effects of turns on single politician

indicators.note: on places the piece named before it after the one named next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
variety turns are acts

explanation.surface: The consequences of performances on a lone MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: impacts are the effects or consequences something has.

clue.text: Watch for ability to judge

explanation.definitionFit: To eye is to watch; an eye for something is a talent for judging it.

clue.text: Country fair e.g. laird might hold back

indicators.note: back says those letters run backwards
might hold says the words contain the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A landowner holding back at a country fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Read FAIREGLAIRD backwards to find the seven letters spanning 'fair e.g. laird'.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Rose possibly to waffle on right

indicators.note: on in a down clue sets the first piece above the second

parts.note: to ramble is to waffle, talk aimlessly

explanation.surface: A rose possibly going on and on at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like the verb (got up) but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing rose with long trailing stems, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Feeling as pride is shattered?

indicators.note: shattered means broken in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The emotion felt when one's pride is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is a feeling of utter hopelessness, an example of an emotion.

clue.text: Vacant school needing cardinal to show manual dexterity

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: a cardinal number such as eight

explanation.surface: An empty school needing a senior churchman to show skill with hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like the churchman but is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is skilful use of the hands, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Expert's finished

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplished pianist is skilled; a task accomplished is completed.

clue.text: Part of vessel featuring in register nowadays

indicators.note: featuring in says the letters appear within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A section of a ship mentioned in a modern register.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship or boat.

clue.text: Parting word from company about returning first-class

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps the second
returning means the letters read backwards

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A goodbye from a firm about coming back in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class is A1, with the figure 1 written as the letter I; 'returning' reverses it and 'about' wraps the company abbreviation round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell is a common informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Four points for intelligence

definitions.meaning: the four compass points north, east, west, south

explanation.walkthrough: The four compass letters N, E, W, S spell the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of information or reports is a synonym of current tidings.

clue.text: Question from church everybody English expects initially

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A query from the church that all of England expects.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to challenge a claim is to question or dispute it.

clue.text: Pretext of chaps on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard, so a word sounding the same

parts.note: chaps are guys

explanation.surface: An excuse given by men speaking on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the guise of something means under its pretence, a false outward show.

clue.text: Put off doctor accepting summer in France

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ete is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: A GP postponing a summer holiday in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deter someone is to discourage or put them off.

clue.text: Gives the green light to restrictions

definitions.meaning: penalties or embargoes imposed on a state

explanation.surface: Approving a set of limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a contronym: it means both approves and penalties, opposite senses.
